blocks.content: The brick layout is generated procedurally from row and column indices. Each brick's pixel position is calculated from its grid position plus a fixed offset:

this.x = BRICK_OFFSET_LEFT + col * (BRICK_WIDTH + BRICK_GAP);
this.y = BRICK_OFFSET_TOP  + row * (BRICK_HEIGHT + BRICK_GAP);
BRICK_OFFSET_LEFT = 25 shifts the entire grid away from the canvas edge. BRICK_GAP = 6 is the spacing between bricks. With 6 columns: 25 + 6 × (70 + 6) = 481px — just within the 500px canvas.
Row color and point value both come from the row index:

this.color  = BRICK_ROW_COLORS[row % BRICK_ROW_COLORS.length];
this.points = (BRICK_ROWS - row) * 10;  // row 0 = 40 pts, row 3 = 10 pts
Top rows are worth more because they are harder to reach.
